note: Names, descriptions and grades are the official PlayStation list, as Exophase and PSNProfiles published it. Every guide below is written for this entry, in our own words, and cites its sources. No trophy here needs online play.

trophies.guide: The Platinum is the last trophy you earn: it pops the moment the other 54 are done, so there is nothing extra to do for it. Work the roadmap in order — story first, then activities, then collectibles — and finish with 100% completion, which is the real gate. Keep the checklist in this guide ticked as you go so nothing is left to hunt at the end.
trophies.name: Vice Got a Price!
steps: Earn the other 54 trophies.
Finish 100% completion last — it is the longest grind.
Check the tracker: when it reads 54 of 54, the Platinum pops.

trophies.guide: This is the opening mission, Gone Fishing, so it comes naturally in the first hour of the story — just play it through to the end. It is story-locked: the trophy is tied to that one mission, so earn it while you play it rather than assuming you can mop it up later. If the mission ends without the trophy, open the mission replay menu before you move deep into the story.
trophies.name: Just Like Paradise
steps: Start the story and play Gone Fishing to its end.
Follow the mission objectives until the mission-complete screen.

trophies.guide: Finish every mission in Chapter 1 and the trophy pops at the chapter close. Chapter trophies are story-locked by definition: they belong to a stretch of the story you play once, so do the side activities of Chapter 1 — including the meditation session tied to Positive Mental Attitude — before the chapter ends. There is no way to earn a chapter trophy without playing that chapter.
trophies.name: Paradise Lost
steps: Play through all of Chapter 1's missions.
Do Chapter 1 side content first — see Positive Mental Attitude.
The trophy pops when the chapter closes.

trophies.guide: Finish every mission in Chapter 2 and the trophy pops at the chapter close. Like every chapter trophy it is story-locked: it can only be earned while you are playing that chapter, so clear the chapter's side activities before the finale mission. Keep an eye on the stranger strands that open up here — they feed the Strangers & Freaks trophy later.
trophies.name: T**s Ass Drug Money
steps: Play through all of Chapter 2's missions.
Clear the chapter's side activities before its final mission.

trophies.guide: Finish every mission in Chapter 3 and the trophy pops at the chapter close. This is the Vice City chapter, so expect the city itself to open up properly here — use the time to bank exploration progress toward The Goodtime State and to try the activities that feed Master of None. As with the other chapter trophies, it is story-locked to this chapter.
trophies.name: Vice City, Baby!
steps: Play through all of Chapter 3's missions.
Use the chapter to explore Vice City and try new activities.

trophies.guide: Finish every mission in Chapter 4 and the trophy pops at the chapter close. This is the last chapter before the finale, so it is the moment to finish every strand finale tied to Andy, Kenton, Billy, Randy and Tyrone — those trophies belong to their final missions, and the story does not wait for them. Do the chapter's side content before its last mission.
trophies.name: Top Of The World, Ma
steps: Play through all of Chapter 4's missions.
Finish the strand finales (Andy, Kenton, Billy, Randy, Tyrone) first.
The trophy pops when the chapter closes.

trophies.guide: Play the final mission to its end and the Gold pops. It is the story's last beat, so before you start it, make sure every story-locked trophy is already earned — the chapter trophies, the named-mission trophies and the five strand finales. Once the credits roll, the clean-up stages (activities, collectibles, 100%) are all that is left.
trophies.name: You Gotta Know When to Get Off
steps: Finish all story-locked trophies before the finale.
Play the final mission to its end.

trophies.guide: Complete the mission Breakfast Run. The trophy is named for the mission itself, so it is story-locked: play the mission and finish it, and the trophy pops at the mission-complete screen. If anything goes wrong mid-mission, restart from the last checkpoint rather than abandoning the run.
trophies.name: Trust
steps: Play the mission Breakfast Run.
Finish it — the trophy pops at the mission-complete screen.

trophies.guide: Complete the mission The Cartel Heist. Heist missions are the big set-pieces, so expect several phases — the trophy only counts a full completion, not a partial run. It is story-locked to this mission, so earn it while you play it.
trophies.name: Break the Bank
steps: Play the mission The Cartel Heist.
Complete every phase to the mission-complete screen.

trophies.guide: Complete the mission Child's Play. The trophy is tied to this one mission, so it is story-locked: finish the mission and it pops. There is nothing extra to collect or do — completion of the mission is the whole requirement.
trophies.name: Family Matters
steps: Play the mission Child's Play.
Finish it — the trophy pops at the mission-complete screen.

trophies.guide: Complete the mission Headliners. Like the other named-mission trophies it is story-locked to that mission — play it through and the trophy pops at the end. Do it during your first run through the story so it is not left to mission replay.
trophies.name: DWNFALL
steps: Play the mission Headliners.
Finish it — the trophy pops at the mission-complete screen.

trophies.guide: Complete the mission VCIA Takedown. The name gives the setting away: this one plays out around Vice City International Airport. It is story-locked to the mission, so finish the mission in your story run. The separate trophy Catch Me If You Can is also set at VCIA — read its guide so you do not miss that one while you are there.
trophies.name: Hi-Jacked
steps: Play the mission VCIA Takedown.
Finish it — the trophy pops at the mission-complete screen.
Check Catch Me If You Can while you are at VCIA.

trophies.guide: Complete the mission Operation Savage Glory. The operation name suggests a heavy combat sequence, so go in stocked and expect a long mission — the trophy only counts a full completion. It is story-locked to this mission.
trophies.name: Snow Storm
steps: Stock up before the mission — it is a long combat sequence.
Play Operation Savage Glory to its end.

trophies.guide: Reach 100% completion — the longest grind on the list and the real gate to the Platinum. What counts toward it is the game's completion checklist: story missions, robberies, gang operations, collectibles, races, stunts, challenges and discoveries. The practical route is to finish the story first, then work the tracker in this guide stage by stage; every other trophy feeds this one, and the last few percent are usually a collectible or a challenge you skipped. Early estimates put the Platinum at roughly 200 to 300 hours, so treat this as a long project, not a weekend.
trophies.name: A Long Road
sources: GTA Culture completion guide, via Heyday (https://heyday.news/articles/gta-6-ps5-trophy-list-platinum-100-percent-b79c5017)
PowerPyx / Push Square platinum-time estimates, via GGRecon (https://www.ggrecon.com/articles/gta-6-trophies-achievements-list-platinum/)
steps: Finish the story and every strand finale.
Clear activities, collectibles and challenges stage by stage.
Watch the in-game completion percentage — the trophy pops at 100%.

trophies.guide: Pull off 250 stunts across Leonida — jumps, near-misses, drifts and air time all count toward the running total. This is a volume trophy, so the fastest route is to fold stunts into everything else you do: take jumps on the way to missions, drift through corners, and use the open world between objectives. The counter is cumulative across the whole game, so there is no need to grind it in one sitting.
trophies.name: Cunning Stunts
steps: Play normally and take every jump and drift you pass.
Use fast cars on open roads to chain air time.
The trophy pops at stunt 250.

trophies.description: Try each type of activity once.
trophies.guide: Try each of the nine activity types once — fishing, racing, the shooting range, bowling, the arcade, drone races, meditation, hunting and whatever else the world offers. Do this early, in Chapter 1, because it doubles as a tour of the side content and unlocks the deeper trophies (The Shootist, Top Fun, Positive Mental Attitude) that each need one activity done properly. One attempt at each type is enough; you do not need to win.
trophies.name: Master of None
steps: Open the activities menu and try one of each type.
One attempt each — nine types, nine tries.
The trophy pops on the ninth type.

trophies.description: Earn a gold medal in all Shooting Range challenges.
trophies.guide: Earn a gold medal in all 42 Shooting Range challenges. This is the skill trophy of the set: each challenge has its own gold threshold, so expect to replay the harder ones until the timing and aim click. Work through the ranges in order, learn each challenge's pattern, and leave the toughest for last when your aim is warm. No other trophy depends on it, so it fits anywhere in the clean-up stage.
trophies.name: The Shootist
steps: Visit a shooting range and work the challenges in order.
Replay any challenge until gold — thresholds are per challenge.
Gold all 42 to pop the trophy.

trophies.description: Win a Top Fun Drone Race at every location.
trophies.guide: Win a Top Fun drone race at all 14 locations. Drone racing is about lines, not speed alone: learn each course's gates, cut the corners the course allows, and use the boost on the straights. Each location counts once, so a win anywhere new is progress — work the map location by location and tick them off in the tracker.
trophies.name: Top Fun
steps: Find the Top Fun drone race at a location and win it.
Repeat at all 14 locations.
The trophy pops on the fourteenth win.

trophies.guide: Win 20 different races. Different is the key word: the same race won twice counts once, so work through the race list rather than farming your favourite. Races span cars, boats and bikes, and each type has its own feel — learn the corners of a new race before you push for the win. Twenty distinct wins is the target, and the tracker shows which ones you have already banked.
trophies.name: Earn Cash, Not Kudos
steps: Enter a race you have not won yet and win it.
Work through the race list — 20 different wins.
The trophy pops on the twentieth distinct win.

trophies.description: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge.
trophies.guide: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge. Cal is the rival angler, so this is a head-to-head: out-fish him on the day, not just catch anything. Pick a good spot, watch the water, and keep your line tight — the challenge is won on the best catch, so patience beats speed. One win against Cal is all it takes.
trophies.name: Baited My Tackle
steps: Find Cal's fishing challenge.
Out-fish him — best catch wins.
One win against Cal pops the trophy.

trophies.guide: Complete one arcade game, start to finish. The arcades are scattered around Leonida and each cabinet is its own little game — pick one, learn its rules, and play it through. Completion means reaching the end, not just starting it, so give yourself a quiet half hour and one focused run.
trophies.name: Stick Fiddler
steps: Find an arcade cabinet.
Play one game through to its end.
Completion pops the trophy.

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Andy.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission for Andy. Strand finales are the end of a character's mission line, so you must play Andy's missions in order until his last one appears — there is no shortcut to a finale. It is story-locked to that final mission, so do it during your story run, before the finale of the game itself.
trophies.name: Road to Rehabilitation
steps: Play Andy's mission strand in order.
Complete his final mission.

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Kenton.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission for Kenton. Like the other strand finales, this one only appears after you have played Kenton's whole mission line in order. It is story-locked to that final mission, so finish it during the story run — the game does not hold strand finales open after the credits.
trophies.name: This Was No Boat Accident
steps: Play Kenton's mission strand in order.
Complete his final mission.

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Billy.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission for Billy. Billy's strand ends with this mission, and the trophy is tied to it alone — play his missions in order until the finale unlocks, then finish it. It is story-locked, so do it before the game's final mission.
trophies.name: The Lone Rider
steps: Play Billy's mission strand in order.
Complete his final mission.

trophies.description: Complete 8 mission strands for strangers across the state of Leonida.
trophies.guide: Complete 8 mission strands for strangers across the state of Leonida. Stranger missions are the open-world encounters marked around the map — each one is a short strand of its own, and eight completed strands is the target. They unlock as you explore, so the practical route is to stop for every stranger marker you pass while you travel, rather than saving them all for the end. The five named strand finales (Andy, Kenton, Billy, Randy, Tyrone) are part of the same world of side characters, so work them together.
trophies.name: Strangers & Freaks
steps: Stop for stranger markers as you explore Leonida.
Complete 8 full stranger strands.
The trophy pops on the eighth.

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Randy.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission for Randy. Randy's strand ends here, and the trophy belongs to that final mission alone — play his missions in order until it unlocks, then finish it. It is story-locked, so earn it during the story run.
trophies.name: Supply & Demand
steps: Play Randy's mission strand in order.
Complete his final mission.

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Tyrone.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission for Tyrone. Tyrone's strand ends with this mission — play his missions in order until the finale appears, then finish it. It is story-locked to that final mission.
trophies.name: Spin On This!
steps: Play Tyrone's mission strand in order.
Complete his final mission.

trophies.description: Meditate at every spot across Leonida.
trophies.guide: Meditate at all 18 spots across Leonida. This is the one trophy on the list that outside reporting singles out as missable: it is tied to a meditation session with Lucia in Chapter 1, so do the Chapter 1 meditation while you are still in Chapter 1 — it may not come back later. After that, work the remaining spots as you explore; meditation spots are quiet places on the map, and the tracker keeps count so you can see which regions are still missing one.
trophies.name: Positive Mental Attitude
sources: GTABase, via GGRecon — tied to a meditation session with Lucia in Chapter 1 (https://www.ggrecon.com/articles/gta-6-trophies-achievements-list-platinum/)
steps: In Chapter 1, do the meditation session with Lucia first.
Then meditate at every other spot across Leonida.
The trophy pops at spot 18.

trophies.description: Hunt a unique animal for Bret.
trophies.guide: Hunt a unique animal for Bret. Bret's hunt is a single target, not a species — find the animal he names, track it, and take it down cleanly. Hunting rewards patience: watch the animal's habits, approach downwind, and take the shot when it holds still. One unique animal is the whole requirement.
trophies.name: Fair Game
steps: Take Bret's hunt and find the unique animal.
Track it and take it down.
One kill pops the trophy.

trophies.guide: Complete 3 collectible card sets. Cards are hidden around Leonida in packs, and a set is only complete when every card in it is found — the hunt is the trophy. Work the map region by region, and use the tracker to note which sets are one card short. Three finished sets is the target, so pick the sets whose cards cluster near places you already visit.
trophies.name: Don't Touch My Deck
steps: Collect card packs as you explore.
Complete 3 full sets.
The trophy pops on the third set.

trophies.guide: WAiNK It at 100 locations. WAiNK is the in-world photo-sharing app, so the requirement is to post from 100 different spots — the game is really asking you to see the whole map. Fold it into exploration: whenever you arrive somewhere new, open WAiNK and post. A hundred posts sounds like a lot, but one per new place adds up fast across a full playthrough.
trophies.name: You WAiNKer!
steps: Post on WAiNK at every new location you reach.
Keep posting as you explore — 100 spots.
The trophy pops on the hundredth post.

trophies.guide: Complete 50 challenges. Challenges are the small feats scattered through every system — stunts, driving, combat, exploration — and they stack up naturally if you play broadly. The practical route is to open the challenges list early, see which ones are nearly done, and finish those first; the last few are the ones that need a deliberate session. Fifty completed is the target.
trophies.name: One Last Thing
steps: Open the challenges list and see what is nearly done.
Finish the near-complete ones first.
The trophy pops at challenge 50.

trophies.description: Lose a 4 star Wanted Level with your partner and escape the heat.
trophies.guide: Lose a 4-star wanted level with your partner and escape the heat. This is a co-op moment in the story: you need your partner beside you, the heat at four stars, and then a clean escape with both of you alive. Lose the cops in the hills or the water, break line of sight, and wait out the search — the trophy pops when the wanted level clears. It is story-locked to the moments your partner is with you, so take the chance when the story gives it.
trophies.name: Hot Together
steps: With your partner beside you, raise the heat to 4 stars.
Break line of sight and lose the cops.
Escape with your partner — the trophy pops when the level clears.

trophies.description: Rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner without losing your Wanted Level.
trophies.guide: Rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner without losing your wanted level. The trick is the back-to-back part: hit one shop, keep the heat, drive straight to the next, and do not let the wanted level drop between robberies. Plan the route first — three shops close together — and keep a fast car waiting. Three in a row, heat held throughout, is the whole requirement.
trophies.name: Retail Therapy
steps: Pick three shops close together and plan the route.
Rob them back-to-back with your partner, heat held.
Three in a row pops the trophy.

trophies.guide: Discover 100 vehicles. Discovery means finding a vehicle type you have not seen before — the game counts distinct vehicles, so variety beats repetition. Drive everything you pass: cars, bikes, boats, trucks and the oddities. A hundred distinct vehicles is the target, and the count climbs fastest when you explore new areas, where the vehicle mix changes.
trophies.name: Whip It Good
steps: Drive every new vehicle type you pass.
Explore new areas — the mix changes by region.
The trophy pops at vehicle 100.

trophies.description: Take down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus.
trophies.guide: Take down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus. Combat Focus slows time, so the requirement is really about lining up five targets in one window: pick a crowded fight, trigger Focus when the enemies cluster, and work through them before it ends. If the fight is thin, wait for a bigger one — a gang shootout or a police stand-off gives you the crowd you need.
trophies.name: Gunslinger
steps: Find a crowded fight with enemies clustered.
Trigger Combat Focus and take down 5 in one window.
Five in one Focus pops the trophy.

trophies.description: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA.
trophies.guide: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA — Vice City International Airport. The trophy is a stunt with a setting: get a plane moving at the airport and leave without a flight plan, in your own style. It is tied to VCIA itself, so do it while the story has you at the airport (see Hi-Jacked) rather than assuming a later visit will offer the same chance.
trophies.name: Catch Me If You Can
steps: Go to VCIA — ideally during the Hi-Jacked mission.
Get a plane moving and depart unscheduled.
The trophy pops on departure.

trophies.guide: Deal with the Rhinos — the tanks. The description is a joke, but the requirement is a fight: take on the military hardware and come out on top. Heavy weapons and distance are your friends; a tank up close is a death sentence, so use cover, rockets and patience. Exactly what counts as dealing with them is in the trophy's own wording — expect a wanted-level shootout to bring them to you.
trophies.name: Challenging Tank
steps: Raise the heat until Rhinos roll in.
Take them on with heavy weapons and cover.
Survive the fight — the trophy pops.

trophies.description: Rob a jewelry store without being detected.
trophies.guide: Rob a jewelry store without being detected. Stealth is the whole requirement: get in, take the goods, and get out with nobody raising the alarm. Study the store first — cameras, guards, sightlines — and go in quiet, at night if you can. If you are spotted, the attempt fails, so restart the approach rather than shooting your way out.
trophies.name: Sneakthief
steps: Scout the jewelry store: cameras, guards, sightlines.
Rob it without being detected.
A clean, unseen robbery pops the trophy.

trophies.guide: Rob 5 bank vaults and escape. Vaults are the big robberies: plan each one, crack the vault, and — the part that matters — escape cleanly afterwards. Five vaults, five escapes. The getaway is half the job, so have the escape route and the fast car ready before you go in, and do not linger once the vault is open.
trophies.name: Maximum Withdrawal
steps: Plan the vault and the escape route first.
Rob the vault and escape cleanly.
Five vaults and five escapes pops the trophy.

trophies.description: Rob an Armored Truck and escape.
trophies.guide: Rob an armored truck and escape. Armored trucks run set routes around Leonida — find one, stop it, crack it, and get away before the response arrives. The escape matters as much as the robbery: have a fast car ready and a route that loses the tail. One truck, one clean escape.
trophies.name: A Classic Blitz Play
steps: Find an armored truck on its route and stop it.
Crack it and escape cleanly.
One truck and one escape pops the trophy.

trophies.guide: Explore all 52 areas of Leonida. This is the map-completion trophy: every named area on the map counts, from Vice City's districts to the swamps and the keys. The practical route is to drive the whole map once, letting the area names tick over as you pass through, and then mop up the last few with the in-game map as your checklist. It pairs naturally with WAiNK posts and vehicle discovery, so do all three on the same road trip.
trophies.name: The Goodtime State
steps: Drive the whole map and let area names tick over.
Check the map for areas you have not entered.
All 52 areas pops the trophy.

trophies.description: Rob an Illegal Operation belonging to each gang.
trophies.guide: Rob an illegal operation belonging to each of the 9 gangs. Every gang runs its own operations around Leonida, and the trophy wants one hit on each gang's turf — nine gangs, nine robberies. Learn which operations belong to whom as you explore, and work the list gang by gang. The operations also feed the 100% completion checklist, so this is progress on two fronts at once.
trophies.name: Pest Control
steps: Find an illegal operation for each of the 9 gangs.
Rob one per gang.
Nine gangs hit pops the trophy.

trophies.description: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach.
trophies.guide: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach. This is one of the ambient trophies: go to Ocean Beach, order a cocktail, and take in the view. There is no trick to it — the game wants you to stop and look at the place. Any beachfront bar with a view of the ocean should do; sit down, order, and the trophy pops.
trophies.name: In The Beginning…
steps: Go to Ocean Beach.
Order a cocktail with a view.
Sit back — the trophy pops.

trophies.description: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style.
trophies.guide: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style. The description is a nod to the series' history: pick a showroom, get a car moving inside it, and drive straight out through the glass. It is a stunt with a setting, so the car and the angle matter — line up on the window, build speed, and go through. One dramatic exit is the whole requirement.
trophies.name: Capital Offense
steps: Find a vehicle showroom.
Line a car up on the glass and build speed.
Smash out — the trophy pops.

trophies.description: Follow-through at the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley.
trophies.guide: Follow through at the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley. Bowling is one of the nine activities, and this trophy wants a proper game there — play a full game at this specific alley and follow through on your throws. It is the alley that matters, not the score, so play the game out and the trophy pops at the end.
trophies.name: Let’s Go Bowling
steps: Go to the Kolt & Associates bowling alley.
Play a full game, following through on each throw.
Finish the game — the trophy pops.

trophies.guide: A partnership with mass appeal. The description is deliberately vague — this is one of the cryptic trophies whose requirement only becomes clear in play. It reads as a moment between the two leads that the wider world notices: keep playing the story with your partner, do the things that build the partnership's public profile, and it should pop on its own. If it has not popped by the finale, it is a clean-up trophy to chase in free roam.
trophies.name: Personal Best
steps: Play the story with your partner and build the partnership.
Watch for a public moment between the leads.
If it has not popped by the finale, chase it in free roam.

trophies.guide: Choices made, for better or worse. The description is cryptic, and the trophy tracks the decisions you make across the game — the small choices as well as the big ones. There is no single moment to aim for: just play the story and the side content, make your calls, and the total builds up. It pops when your choices reach the number the game counts, so a full playthrough that engages with the choices should earn it naturally.
trophies.name: Actions Speak Louder
steps: Play the story and side content, making your calls.
Keep engaging with choices as they come.
The trophy pops when your choices reach the count.

trophies.guide: Second time's the charm. The description tells the story: something that failed the first time works on the second try. Expect a moment where a plan goes wrong and the game gives you another shot — take it, and the trophy pops. It is the kind of trophy you earn by playing on rather than reloading an old save after a failure.
trophies.name: Bad Luck, I Guess
steps: Play on after a failed attempt instead of reloading.
Take the second try when the game offers it.
Success on the second try pops the trophy.

trophies.guide: What the hell just happened? This is the strangest trophy on the list, and the description is the only clue: something unexpected has to happen to you. It reads as a random world event — the kind of odd encounter that finds you while you are doing something else. Keep exploring, keep your eyes open for the weird, and it should find you. If it has not popped by the end of the story, it is a free-roam hunt.
trophies.name: The Truth Is Out There
steps: Explore Leonida and watch for strange events.
Keep playing — the event finds you.
Witness it and the trophy pops.

trophies.description: Bowl 'em over with a melee drive-by.
trophies.guide: Bowl 'em over with a melee drive-by. This is a driving stunt with a melee twist: hit someone with a melee attack from a moving vehicle, bowling them over. Speed and timing are everything — line up the pass, swing as you go by, and keep driving. One clean melee drive-by is the requirement.
trophies.name: Ten Pin
steps: Get a vehicle moving past a pedestrian.
Swing a melee attack as you pass.
One clean hit pops the trophy.

trophies.description: Earn $250,000 laundering Marked Bills through your contacts.
trophies.guide: Earn $250,000 laundering marked bills through your contacts. Marked bills come from robberies and heists, and your contacts turn them into clean money — the trophy counts the total laundered, not what you keep. Robberies feed it directly, so work the vaults, trucks and shops, then launder the take through your contacts. A quarter of a million laundered is the target.
trophies.name: Dime on the Dollar
steps: Rob vaults, trucks and shops for marked bills.
Launder the take through your contacts.
$250,000 laundered pops the trophy.

trophies.guide: Spend $100,000 across all shops. This is a spending trophy, not an earning one: the money goes on clothes, weapons, food, car mods and everything the shops sell. It adds up naturally across a full playthrough, but if you are frugal, the fastest route is a shopping run — buy the expensive things you actually want, like cars and weapon upgrades, and the total climbs. A hundred thousand spent is the target.
trophies.name: Treat Yo Self
steps: Shop as you play — clothes, weapons, cars, mods.
If you are short, do a shopping run on big items.
$100,000 spent pops the trophy.

trophies.guide: Purchase all 8 garage properties. Garages are the properties that store your vehicle collection, and the trophy wants all eight owned. They are bought with in-game money, so the practical route is to buy them as your funds allow during the story, and mop up the last ones with robbery money in the clean-up stage. Eight garages owned is the whole requirement.
trophies.name: Little Boxes
steps: Buy garage properties as your funds allow.
Mop up the last ones with robbery money.
All 8 owned pops the trophy.

trophies.description: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app.
trophies.guide: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app. Scooter Bros is the in-world rideshare app, and registering a vehicle means adding it to the fleet — drive a vehicle you own to the app's drop-off and sign it in. Ten different vehicles registered is the target, so use the collection you build up across the game rather than buying ten at once.
trophies.name: On the Spot
steps: Own a vehicle and open the Scooter Bros app.
Register it to the fleet.
Register 10 vehicles — the trophy pops.
